headline: Single-cell methods borrow structure across modalities and models to assign clones and cell identities
label: Cross Modal Single Cell Inference
summary: KLONE links scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones, while ensemble, transformer and distillation methods push cell-type and population labeling.
synthesis: The one explicitly cross-modal item is KLONE, which assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones using cross-modal Pearson similarity and a per-clone k-NN ensemble designed for class imbalance. Most other items stay within scRNA-seq and address label inference by other means: scBoost stacks existing methods in an AdaBoost-inspired ensemble, scDNM uses a dendritic neuron model with learnable synaptic thresholds, a fine-tuned Geneformer-V1 feeds class-probability matrices into unsupervised clustering for de novo populations, and scAdaG2M distills graph models into an MLP with AdaBoost reweighting. scGPL combines graph topology with pairwise TF-target modeling for GRN inference. Sequence-level items (RawMod, DeepHel, the CNN for coding versus intergenomic DNA) are peripheral. The new element is ensemble and imbalance-aware inference, rather than a single shared cancer-focused approach.
